question: The chemical name of Plaster of Paris is ___________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**calcium sulphate hemihydrate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Plaster of Paris** is chemically known as **calcium sulphate hemihydrate (CaSO₄·½H₂O)**.
 
• It is produced by heating gypsum (calcium sulphate dihydrate) to a temperature of about 150°C.
 
• When mixed with water, Plaster of Paris rehydrates and hardens, making it useful for casting molds, sculptures, and medical casts.
 
• It is widely used in construction for coating walls and ceilings and in art for making sculptures and decorative items.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gypsum**

 
 
• Gypsum is a naturally occurring mineral composed of calcium sulphate dihydrate (CaSO₄·2H₂O).
 
• It is used in the manufacture of plaster, drywall, cement, and as a soil conditioner in agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Setting Time**
 
 
• Plaster of Paris sets quickly, typically within 10 to 15 minutes, after being mixed with water.
 
• The setting time can be adjusted by adding various chemicals to the mixture.
 
 
 
• **Medical Uses**
 
 
• It is extensively used in orthopedics for making casts to immobilize broken bones while they heal.
 
• It provides a rigid structure that conforms to the shape of the injured limb.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance**
 
 
• Plaster of Paris has been used since ancient times, with evidence of its use in Egyptian tombs and Roman buildings.
 
• Its name originates from the large deposits of gypsum found in Paris, France.
